summary: As of Sunday, September 27, before the U.S. open, there is no U.S. cash session today, so the relevant Nasdaq setup is the risk being carried into Monday rather than a same-day pre-market tape. Friday ended constructively: the Nasdaq Composite rose about 0.48%, with Microsoft and other AI-related technology shares helping buyers overcome continued concern about high oil prices and Treasury yields. The 10-year Treasury yield finished near 5.16% after touching roughly 5.23%, its highest level since 2007, while oil fell about 3% on hopes that U.S.-Iran diplomacy could ease the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. index futures are not yet in their normal Sunday-evening trading session, so there is no reliable live Nasdaq futures signal to use at the 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff.

That Friday relief now faces a meaningful weekend counterweight. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the fighting, while Iran continued to argue that reopening the waterway depends on its conditions being met through negotiation. That weakens the de-escalation assumption that helped oil and bond markets on Friday and makes the first oil, Treasury and Nasdaq-futures reaction later Sunday especially important. The supportive side remains resilient AI/mega-cap demand and Friday's ability to rally despite a historically high long-term yield; the principal risk is that renewed Middle East tension sends crude and inflation expectations higher again, pulling Treasury yields back toward or through Friday's extremes and compressing technology valuations.

events.title: 1. U.S.-Iran / Strait of Hormuz diplomacy — ongoing
events.detail: The most important Nasdaq catalyst today is geopolitical rather than scheduled macro data. Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz and end the fighting, removing some of the optimism that helped crude fall on Friday. Any clarification through mediators, renewed negotiating signal, military escalation or threat to Gulf shipping could materially change the oil-and-yields backdrop before Monday's U.S. session.

events.title: 2. Sunday reopening of global risk markets — later today
events.detail: Because U.S. cash markets are closed, the first market verdict on the weekend Iran news will come as oil and U.S. index futures reopen later Sunday. For Nasdaq, the important cross-market confirmation is whether crude rebounds sharply and whether Treasury yields follow inflation expectations higher; a contained oil response would make Friday's technology resilience more credible.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the constructive Monday scenario is that weekend diplomacy remains alive despite Trump's rejection, oil gives back any initial risk premium, the 10-year stays below Friday's roughly 5.23% extreme, and AI/semiconductor leadership continues to absorb the rates pressure. The downside scenario is a renewed crude spike or escalation around Hormuz that pushes inflation expectations and Treasury yields higher together; with long-duration technology already facing a 10-year yield above 5%, that combination would be the clearest threat to Friday's rebound. Sunday-evening oil and Nasdaq futures should therefore matter more than the absence of scheduled U.S. data today.
keyTimes: There is no U.S. cash-market open today because it is Sunday. The next regular U.S. cash session opens Monday, September 28 at 9:30 ET, which is 16:30 in Istanbul. The most important near-term timing is the reopening of oil and U.S. index futures later Sunday, followed by Monday's cash open; unscheduled U.S.-Iran and Strait of Hormuz headlines remain the dominant catalyst until then.
